AD Homelab Overview Architecture Access model Build timeline Troubleshooting Validation
Windows Server 2022 · Active Directory · VMware Workstation

An enterprise-style Windows domain, built and broken on purpose

A two-VM homelab with a domain controller and a domain-joined Windows 11 client. It covers identity, DNS, DHCP, file access, Group Policy, software deployment and account security. It also records the faults found along the way and how each was fixed.

Domain: LamHomeLab.local DC01 · Windows Server 2022 CLIENT01 · Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC Eval 24H2 Host-only network · 192.168.10.0/24

1 · Architecture

What is in the lab

Everything runs on one VMware Workstation host. The final design is a single isolated Layer 2 segment, with Windows Server providing DNS, DHCP and AD for the clients.

Switch between the first build and the final design to see what changed.

Final design: each VM has one network adapter on VMnet1. Windows Server DHCP is the only DHCP service on the segment.

Domain controller

DC01 — AD DS, DNS, DHCP and file services on a static 192.168.10.10.

Client

CLIENT01 — Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC Evaluation (24H2), joined to LamHomeLab.local, receives 192.168.10.100 from DHCP.

Network

VMnet1 host-only with VMware DHCP off. VMware's own subnet for VMnet1 is 192.168.230.0/24; the lab addressing is set on the guests and served by Windows DHCP.

DHCP scope

192.168.10.100 – 192.168.10.200 (101 addresses). Option 015 = LamHomeLab.local.

2 · Identity and access

How people and permissions are organised

Departments are Organisational Units. Access is granted to security groups, never to individual users, so onboarding a person means adding them to a group.

3 · Build timeline

How the lab was built, step by step

Ten phases in the order they were done. Click any screenshot to enlarge it. Each phase carries an evidence badge so it is clear what was captured and what was only performed.

Evidence badges: Verified Partial Documented Performed, not captured
00

Build the virtual machines

Verified

Create the two VMs that the rest of the lab depends on.

  • DC01: Windows Server 2022, 4 GB RAM, 2 vCPU, 60 GB disk.
  • The first build used a NAT adapter to reach installation media; it was removed later (see Troubleshooting).
  • CLIENT01: Windows 11 IoT Enterprise LTSC Evaluation 24H2, a clean machine before joining the domain.
  • Server Manager's Add Roles and Features wizard was used to add roles.
01

Active Directory: domain, OUs and groups

Verified

Promote DC01 and model the company: one OU and one security group per department.

  • Domain LamHomeLab.local created on DC01.
  • OUs: Finance, HR, IT, Marketing, Sales. Groups: Finance Users, HR Users, IT Users, Marketing Users, Sales Users.
  • GG_ControlPanel_Restricted groups the four non-IT groups so one policy can target them.
02

DNS and domain join

Zone verified · lookups not captured

Give the domain a name service, then bring the client into it.

  • Forward lookup zone LamHomeLab.local with the _msdcs zone, Active Directory integrated.
  • DC01 resolves to 192.168.10.10 (host record and zone NS/SOA).
  • CLIENT01 uses the DC as its DNS server and was joined to LamHomeLab.local.

Evidence note: nslookup and ping dc01 from the client were run and checked on screen, but no screenshot was kept. The join dialog capture shows the workflow with LAMHOMELAB.LOCAL entered, not the completed join.

03

File server and shares

Partial

Publish department folders and control access by group.

  • Folders under C:\CompanyShares: Finance, HR, IT, Marketing, Sales.
  • Finance published as \\DC01\Finance; share level is Everyone / Full Control, so the real restriction is NTFS.
  • Finance Users added to the NTFS permissions; removing inherited Users required turning inheritance off first.
  • Effective access is the most restrictive of share and NTFS permissions.

Evidence note: the final NTFS permission list and the Finance-allowed / IT-denied test results were checked on screen but not captured. The two NTFS images are low-resolution crops.

04

Group Policy: map the Finance drive

Partial

Map \\DC01\Finance as F: for Finance only, with no logon script.

  • GPO Finance - Map Network Drive uses a Drive Maps preference.
  • Item-level targeting: the user is a member of the security group LAMHOMELAB\Finance Users.
  • The drive first failed to appear; the fix was targeting plus gpupdate /force and a fresh sign-in.

Evidence note: gpresult lists the GPO as applied (shown in phase 05). A screenshot of F: in Explorer was not captured.

05

Group Policy: restrict Control Panel

Verified

Block Control Panel for everyone except IT, using group-based security filtering.

  • GPO Block - Control panel linked at the domain, setting Prohibit access to Control Panel and PC settings = Enabled.
  • Security filtering limited to GG_ControlPanel_Restricted.
  • First attempt did not apply: the target lacked Read on the GPO (see Troubleshooting, case 2).
  • After the fix, opening Control Panel shows "This operation has been cancelled due to restrictions".
  • The IT user's whoami /groups lists IT Users and not the restricted group, so IT is unaffected.
06

Account lockout and recovery

Partial

Reproduce a lockout as a user would see it, then recover the account as an administrator.

  • Domain password and lockout settings are set in the Default Domain Policy.
  • Locked account on the client: "The referenced account is currently locked out and may not be logged on to."
  • Recovery through ADUC: Reset Password with Unlock the user's account.
  • PowerShell: Search-ADAccount -LockedOut; the first attempts failed with a parameter-set error until the switch was supplied.

Evidence note: the lockout policy values and the output of Unlock-ADAccount were not captured.

07

Software deployment with Group Policy

Install verified · package settings not captured

Install 7-Zip on the client centrally, with no manual setup.

  • 7-Zip MSI assigned through Computer Configuration → Software Installation.
  • 7-Zip 26.02 (x64) appears in the client's Installed apps.
  • The MSI itself is not stored in the repository.
08

DHCP and network design

Verified

Move addressing from VMware to Windows Server DHCP on an isolated segment.

  • DHCP role installed on DC01; scope 192.168.10.0/24 with range .100 – .200.
  • Server bound to the LAN-Domain adapter at 192.168.10.10.
  • Scope options set: 006 DNS servers and 015 DNS domain name LamHomeLab.local. The capture also lists further entries.
  • CLIENT01 receives 192.168.10.100; the lease shows on DC01.
  • VMware Virtual Network Editor: VMnet1 is host-only with DHCP off.
09

Troubleshooting the DHCP failure

Documented

The client got a 169.254.x.x address and the server never saw its requests. The full investigation is in the next section.

4 · Troubleshooting

Three problems, and how each was solved

Each case follows the same pattern: what was seen, what was checked, the root cause, the fix, and the result.

The client could not get a DHCP lease

Symptom

CLIENT01 shows 169.254.56.151 (APIPA). ipconfig /renew times out. No lease on DC01.

Checked

DHCP service, authorisation, scope, options and binding, then VMware DHCP.

Isolated

With a temporary static IP the client could ping DC01, so the link and server were fine.

Root cause

A second NAT adapter added an unintended network path and complicated DHCP broadcast delivery.

Fixed

One VMnet1 NIC per VM. Client leased 192.168.10.100 from Windows DHCP.

What the checks showed

  • Get-Service DHCPServer → Running
  • Get-DhcpServerv4Binding → LAN-Domain, 192.168.10.10, True
  • One scope, 101 addresses, 0 in use
  • Get-DhcpServerv4Statistics → Discovers = 0: the server never received a request
  • ipconfig /renew → request has timed out
Get-Service DHCPServer
Get-DhcpServerv4Binding
Get-DhcpServerv4Statistics
ipconfig /renew

Reading the evidence

The server was healthy and listening, yet it counted zero Discover packets. That moved the problem from the DHCP configuration to the network path between the client and the server.

The evidence supports a topology / broadcast-domain fault. It does not by itself prove a duplicate-address conflict. The adapter-removal step was not captured; the failing and final states were.

Takeaway: DHCP depends on broadcasts, so it depends on the topology. When the server shows no Discovers, look at the network path before the scope.

A restricted user could still open Control Panel

Symptom

The GPO was enabled, linked and security filtered, yet a Finance user could open Control Panel.

Checked

Policy setting, user's OU and groups, gpupdate /force, gpresult /r, GPO delegation.

Found

The Control Panel GPO was missing from the user's applied-policy list.

Root cause

The filtered target had no Read permission on the GPO, so it could not process it.

Fixed

Read restored, Apply Group Policy kept. After a new session Control Panel was blocked.

Takeaway: check scope, Read and Apply Group Policy as three separate conditions, and use gpresult to confirm what really applied.

The Finance drive did not appear

Symptom

F: was missing after gpupdate /force and a sign-out / sign-in.

Checked

The GPO link and the user's Finance group membership.

Changed

Added item-level targeting on Finance Users to the drive mapping.

Cause

The first evidence pointed to a linking or targeting problem.

Result

The drive appeared as F:; gpresult lists the GPO as applied.

Evidence note: a screenshot of F: in Explorer was not captured.

Takeaway: after changing policy, refresh and start a new user session before judging the result.
